result.summary:
Re-derived, not trusted, against the actual code (git diff master...HEAD, all 14 changed/new apps/bot files read in full) and both design artefacts (docs/agents/design/REQ-031.md, REQ-031-schema.md). Design-system compliance: N/A, confirmed -- this is a bot-only change (apps/bot/**), no src/public/ touched, no visual/CSS component exists for the bot surface (design §9 states this explicitly and the diff confirms it: zero references to `docs/Design system for AI agents/` tokens/classes anywhere in the 14 changed files).

Specific checks requested, each independently verified:

1. FIELD-MATCH RECHECK (the rework's entire point) -- CONFIRMED IMPLEMENTED, not dropped. Read apps/bot/src/handlers/feedback.ts:267 directly: `makeFeedbackTextReplyHandler`'s step-8 gate is `if (step.kind !== "feedback-field" || step.field === "nps" || step.field !== parsed.field) { return; }` -- the third clause (`step.field !== parsed.field`) is exactly design §6.3 step 8's fix: a stale reply to an older, already-superseded prompt for one field (encoded in that prompt's own 'Feedback field: ' line, parsed via `parseFeedbackReplyContext` in domain/feedback.ts) is a no-op when the freshly-derived `step.field` names a different, currently-expected sibling field, rather than being silently written to the wrong column. Matches design §1.2/§6.3 exactly.

2. NPS-TRIGGERS-INSERT SEMANTICS -- CONFIRMED. `writeFeedbackNps` (domain/feedback.ts) is the only function in the entire diff that calls `db.insert(feedback)` -- grepped/read every write function: `writeFeedbackOptionalField` and `markFeedbackFieldSkipped` are both `db.update(feedback)...where(eq(feedback.registrationId, ...))`, never insert. Traced every call site (handlers/feedback.ts's three handlers, scheduler/feedbackJobs.ts's compose function): the only path that can create a row is a genuine 0-10 NPS button tap via `makeFeedbackNpsCallbackHandler`'s gated call to `writeFeedbackNps`. No optional-field write is reachable before a row exists (§2.2's ordering, re-derived fresh in every handler) -- skipping NPS structurally creates nothing.

3. BROADCAST-OPT-IN GATE -- CONFIRMED matches AC5. `determineFeedbackFlowStep` (domain/feedback.ts) gates on `broadcastOptInAskedAt === null`, never on `broadcastOptIn`'s boolean value. `writeBroadcastOptInAnswer` (domain/user.ts) is confirmed the only function anywhere in apps/bot/src that writes either `users.broadcast_opt_in` or `users.broadcast_opt_in_asked_at`, writing both columns in the same UPDATE statement.

4. SCHEDULED JOBS -- CONFIRMED. `selectRegistrationsForFeedbackRequest` (scheduler/feedbackJobs.ts) gates on `isNotNull(registrations.checkedInAt)` -- AC1's entire mechanism, an admitted-but-never-checked-in registration is excluded by construction from ever reaching this job. `selectRegistrationsForFeedbackReminder` additionally excludes any registration with an existing `feedback` row via `notInArray(registrations.id, existingFeedbackRegistrationIds)`. Both sends route through `sendLedgeredNotification` with distinct `NotificationKind`s (`feedback_request` vs `feedback_reminder`, confirmed as the only addition to the `NotificationKind` union in domain/notification.ts), each independently governed by the existing REQ-025 ledger's `UNIQUE(registration_id, kind)` constraint -- re-running the T+24h job at T+48h re-selects the same untouched candidate but the ledger insert collides, producing `skipped-already-sent`, never a second send. This satisfies AC4.

5. MIGRATION vs SCHEMA ARTEFACT -- CONFIRMED byte-for-byte equivalent (statement order differs trivially -- the ALTER TABLE users statement is emitted before the FK/index statements rather than after, which is semantically inert -- but every column type, NOT NULL, DEFAULT, CHECK, and constraint name in apps/bot/drizzle/0006_smiling_leader.sql matches REQ-031-schema.md §6's expected-shape block exactly: chk_feedback_nps_range, uq_feedback_registration_id, the FK with ON DELETE restrict, text[] for topic_votes, three *_skipped booleans NOT NULL DEFAULT false). schema.ts's feedback table definition (apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts) matches column-for-column.

6. SCOPE DISCIPLINE -- CONFIRMED. `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/handlers/staff.ts` produces zero output -- staff.ts (ISS-0020) is untouched. Full diff stat contains only the 14 files the design/handoff named plus the migration pair, i18n locale files, and design/handoff bookkeeping files -- no stray file, apps/web untouched.

7. TEST-INFRASTRUCTURE FLAKINESS FINDING -- INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED, not taken on trust. Ran `DATABASE_URL=... npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` myself against the live scratch Postgres on this branch: 308/308 passed, matching BACKEND-DEV's report. To test the pre-existing attribution independently (route 2 of core-directives' Failure Attribution rule), created a separate git worktree at 18f176c (the direct parent commit, i.e. the pre-implementation state), symlinked node_modules to avoid a redundant install, and ran the bare `npx vitest run` (no flag) there against the same scratch DB: 109 failed / 199 passed, with the identical failure signature BACKEND-DEV reported (`deadlock detected` and FK-violation errors from concurrent TRUNCATE calls racing across DB-backed test files). This independently confirms the flakiness reproduces with zero WF02-REQ-031 code applied -- genuinely pre-existing, not introduced or worsened by this diff. Worktree removed afterward (`git worktree remove --force`) and the main working tree verified back to a clean `git status` state.

8. LINT/BUILD -- RE-RUN MYSELF, not trusted from BACKEND-DEV's report. `npm run lint -w apps/bot` -> exit 0, zero problems. `npm run build -w apps/bot` -> exit 0, tsc clean. Both re-run a second time after an incident (see below) to confirm the working tree was fully intact.

Additional checks per REVIEWER's own gate: no domain logic found inside a grammY handler body -- handlers/feedback.ts only sequences calls (resolve identity, derive step, gate a write, advance the flow) and every actual rule (field ordering, skip semantics, ownership derivation) lives in domain/feedback.ts, domain/registration.ts, domain/user.ts, satisfying decisions/0004. No `now()`/`current_timestamp` found in any time-dependent predicate -- every write function and every selection query in scheduler/feedbackJobs.ts takes `evaluationTime`/`at` as an explicit parameter (grepped the full diff for `now()`; the only occurrences are `defaultNow()` column defaults on `created_at`/`updated_at`, the explicitly exempted audit/bookkeeping case per decisions/0006). No npm workspace was added/renamed/removed and no build-output location changed (`git diff master...HEAD -- '**/package.json'` is empty) -- the Dockerfile-verification step (REVIEWER's own gate item 7) does not apply here, so no scratch `docker build` was required or run. Migration is additive-only (CREATE TABLE, two ADD COLUMN statements) -- no personal-data column is dropped or rewritten, so no SECURITY-REVIEWER S13 sign-off is owed on the migration itself before this gate (SECURITY-REVIEWER's own broader S1/S3/S11/S13 pass is still the mandatory next step for apps/bot/** per this gate's own routing rule).

INCIDENT DURING REVIEW (disclosed per Instruction Precedence's 'never resolve a conflict silently' and the personal operating rules' concurrent-session reporting duty): while independently verifying the flakiness finding, a `git worktree add`/`remove --force` cycle I ran against a scratch worktree (with node_modules symlinked back into the main repo to avoid a redundant install) coincided with apps/bot/ and apps/web/ disappearing from disk in the MAIN working tree (still tracked by git, not committed-away -- `git status` showed them as unstaged deletions). A concurrent commit (969f175, 'chore(issues): file ISS-0027...') from a separate ORCH session landed on this same branch during my review, confirming another session was active against this same working directory at the same time; I cannot rule out an interaction between my worktree/symlink operation and that concurrency as the mechanism, though the exact cause is unconfirmed. Recovered immediately and fully via `git restore apps/` (working-tree-only damage, nothing committed or pushed was affected) -- re-verified `git status` clean, `git diff master...HEAD --stat` unchanged from before the incident, and re-ran lint/build clean afterward. No data was lost; flagging this so a future REVIEWER avoids symlinking real node_modules into a scratch worktree used alongside `git worktree remove --force`, and so the user is aware another session was concurrently active on this exact repo path during this run.

issues.title: REVIEWER's own scratch-worktree verification method (symlinking real node_modules into a `git worktree add` scratch checkout, then `git worktree remove --force`) coincided with the main working tree's apps/bot and apps/web directories being emptied on disk
issues.description: While independently re-verifying BACKEND-DEV's pre-existing-flakiness attribution via `git worktree add /tmp/<scratch> 18f176c` + symlinked node_modules + `git worktree remove --force`, the main repo's apps/bot/ and apps/web/ source trees were found emptied on disk immediately after the worktree removal (git status showed them as unstaged deletions -- recovered in full via `git restore apps/`, nothing committed or pushed was lost). A concurrent commit from a separate ORCH session (969f175) landed on this same branch during the same window, confirming another session was active against this exact working directory concurrently. The causal mechanism (my worktree/symlink operation vs. the concurrent session vs. some other interaction) is not confirmed. Recommend future REVIEWER/BACKEND-DEV runs avoid symlinking the main repo's real node_modules into a scratch git worktree, and that ORCH/core-directives consider whether `git worktree remove --force` is safe to use against worktrees that contain symlinks back into the main tree.
